name: FlexGlue
plain: FlexGlue (ETH Zurich and partners, 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: ALIKED keypoints, DINOv3 ConvNeXt features and a transformer that predicts where each keypoint lands in the other photo; keypoint index pairs. MIT; DINOv3 backbone weights under the DINOv3 licence.
summary: FlexGlue (Lindenberger, Sarlin, Miksik and Pollefeys 2026): sparse feature matching from dense features. ALIKED finds up to 2048 keypoints per image at a 1024-pixel long side, a DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B describes each image at 512 x 512, nine transformer layers (rotary self-attention, cross-attention) relate both feature maps, and a head predicts where each keypoint lands in the other image; mutual nearest neighbours of keypoints and predictions are the matches. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their confidence.

papers.title: FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation

no_kernels_reason: not implemented: data-dependent keypoint and match counts
licence_notes: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone weights (`extractor.backbone.*`): the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers them; read it before commercial use.
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the keypoint counts differ per image.
No exportable module: the keypoint and match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).
Upstream's sparse mode only: no RoMa v2 refiner, no dense or sampled matches and no covisibility score.
Two resizes per image as upstream: ALIKED sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

variants.name: aliked-flexglue

licence.training_note: FlexGlue: the README states no training data and the training code is not released (see the paper). The DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B backbone was pretrained on LVD-1689M (Meta, not released); ALIKED was trained on MegaDepth.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0052 and p99 <= 0.012 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).
